transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-21 16:00 PDT
Duration: 1h 4m
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Tomás (Redwood SE), Maya (CSM), Priya (Orion Head ML), Ben (Infra), Angela (CTO), Samir (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick kickoff demo to align on model-catalog selection sprint. Walk through Redwood Console catalog filters, API sampling, and Optimize suggestions for batch/quantization. Agree on prompts, bench window, and data sharing. Discuss hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private VPC) and compatibility matrix requirements.

Topics covered:
- Console: model shortlist, compat filters (architecture, quantization, KC cache), kernel mapping
- API: sampling, streaming, token accounting for cost estimates
- Optimize: batch recommendations, prefix cache, fallback routing policies
- Bench plan: workload slices, P50/P95 latency targets, accuracy/ROUGE-like metrics
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this short, um, kickoff for the catalog fit sprint with Orion, and i'll hand to Tomás to open the console and run through a quick demo
[00:12] Tomás: cool thanks lena, hi priya, ben, angela, samir, i'll share my screen... (screen noises) so first thing i do is filter by model family, we're looking at open LLMs primarily, i've got filters for parameter count, seq len, and kernel compatibility. you'll see a compatibility score that factors in runtime kernels and quantization maturity
[00:38] Priya: quick question, when you say kernel compatibility is that specific to a gpu type or to the compiled kernel? we mostly run on A100 today but targeting H100 in next quarter
[00:46] Tomás: great question, it's a combination — per-model kernel support is mapped to hardware profile (A100, H100, L4) and the runtime will select the best kernel. note there are fallbacks. sometimes the score dips when a quantized path hasn't been exercised on a particular kernel
[01:02] Ben: that fallback story is important for us. we can't have noisier P95 spikes during payroll/critical jobs. how does the router decide between a cheaper quantized variant and a more expensive fp16 run
[01:12] Lena: we typically see customers set policy by latency SLO + cost target. Redwood Optimize suggests a batching/quantization combo and a routing policy; you can set hard SLOs that trigger fallback to the higher-fidelity model variant if latency would be exceeded
[01:27] Angela (overlapping): and for data residency, like audit logs and retention, how does that work in Dedicated vs Hosted?
[01:33] Maya: Hosted stores logs for 30 days by default, dedicated can be configured to push logs to your S3 in-region, and private VPC gives you full control of retention — we also integrate with your KMS for envelope encryption
[01:44] Tomás: back to the console, here's an example shortlist i made for you: two LLaMA-derived 13b variants, a Llama3-ish 7b quantized candidate, and a distilled long-context model. i've annotated each row with bench notes — e.g., token / s throughput in our internal run and an accuracy delta on your prompt subset (we used an internal proxy set)
[02:05] Priya: hmm those proxies are okay but our prompts are more instruction heavy and include many code snippets and tables. will that change the accuracy delta you expect
[02:13] Tomás: yes, and that's why the next step is super important — we need your representative set. our accuracy column is only as good as the prompts. also the kernel mapping can flip for code-heavy tokens since sequence chunking and kv-cache ops behave differently
[02:30] Samir: when you run the bench, do you do end-to-end including our app tokens and network RTT? we need realistic latency measurement not just inference p50 on the box
[02:38] Tomás: we can run both. Option A is runtime-only bench (inference latency + token throughput). Option B is an integrated bench with your network path via a dedicated tunnel (we can schedule a short window for peered VPC test). We'll note both results side-by-side
[02:54] Ben: VPC peering will require a 2 hour maintenance window for allowlist. can we do that after we've narrowed to 2-3 candidates
[02:59] Lena: totally. plan is we pick a shortlist and then schedule the peered bench for the top 2.
[03:06] Priya: what about token cost estimates? our finance team will want predicted cost per 10k sessions.
[03:11] Maya: in the console we show token-level breakdown per route. Redwood Optimize gives cost per token estimates after simulated batch sizing. we can produce a per-10k-session estimate once we have average prompt lengths and response size distributions
[03:28] Angela: are there any gotchas with quantized weights plus long context? we've seen hallucinations increase with some 4-bit variants
[03:35] Tomás: yeah there is a quality trade-off; our bench includes a quality-regression check that runs your eval prompts and flags regressions beyond thresholds. for long context we also test kv-cache eviction behavior and kernel precision under sustained decode
[03:49] Priya: i want to call out success criteria: for us it's 1) accuracy within 3% of our current closed model baseline on intent classification, 2) p95 latency < 450ms at 30 RPS during steady state, and 3) cost reduction of at least 20% per token.
[04:07] Lena: got it, we will bake that into the bench and SOW.
[04:12] Tomás: quick demo of the API — you can spin up a model route, pin a particular variant, and enable automatic fallback. here's a sample curl: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-open-13b-q4","prompt":"<your prompt>","max_tokens":256,"stream":true}'

[04:32] Ben: does your streaming keep a persistent http/2 connection? we want to multiplex sessions
[04:36] Tomás: we support chunked streaming over HTTP/1.1 and h2. For high concurrency we recommend HTTP/2 with persistent connections, and we have SDKs that manage connection pooling
[04:45] Priya: one more on metrics, can we get token-level attribution per user id for debugging?
[04:51] Maya: yes, audit logs can be enriched with token and request metadata, we can send them to your log destination with PII redaction rules applied
[04:58] Angela: what level of RBAC do you support? we need separation between cost visibility and model update permissions
[05:04] Tomás: RBAC is role-based and scoping is per-team and per-route; admin roles can change model pins, cost-only roles can view dashboards and usage but not deploy changes
[05:13] Priya: can we see an example compatibility matrix export?
[05:16] Tomás: sure, i exported one while prepping — i'll paste the link in the chat: (link) https://redwood.app/s/exports/orion-compat-20270421.csv — it includes model, architecture, quant flags (q4/q8), kernels supported, estimated token throughput, and a qualitative note on eval match
[05:33] Samir: i click the csv and it's showing kernel names like cuBLASX_v2.3 and then something like rtx-kernel-optim, some of those are unfamiliar
[05:39] Tomás: couple reasons — our internal names for compiled kernels sometimes differ, and the CSV includes a mapping table. we'll include a legend in the export. also some entries are heuristics for new kernels we plan to test on H100
[05:51] Priya: do you run nightly regression checks when models are upgraded/pulled? we have a strict policy for model drift detection
[05:57] Lena: Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals tied to a prompt set; you can set alert thresholds. for Dedicated customers we can run in your environment as well and surface regressions through the Console with a regression timeline
[06:12] Ben: how does pricing for dedicated burst vs hosted look if we want a guaranteed p95 and 99SLA during payroll windows
[06:18] Maya: two levers: reserved capacity for baseline (monthly commit) and burst capacity for spikes. SLA pricing depends on committed throughput and region. we'll scope an estimate once we know target RPS and required headroom
[06:29] Angela: ok let's talk timeline and deliverables briefly.
[06:33] Lena: plan: 1) Redwood sends shortlist + compat export (tomás) by 4/23, 2) Orion uploads prompts by 4/28, 3) bench run + peered test in week of 5/3, 4) bench results review + pilot SOW draft week of 5/10.
[06:47] Priya: that works. also please include a privacy note for the bench dataset usage.
[06:51] Maya: noted, we'll attach a short data handling appendix to the SOW.
[06:55] Lena: great — any final quick Qs?
[06:58] Priya: nothing else from me. thanks for the demo, tomás was helpful.
[07:02] Ben: likewise.
[07:03] Tomás: cool, i'll post the export and a short runner-up notes doc in the chat after the call; also i'll include a small sample bench plan with the exact workloads we will run
[07:12] Lena: awesome thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench windows. bye everyone.
